Medicaid’s real problem isn’t funding—it’s waste. The Department of Health and Human Services’ budget ballooned from $1.2T to $1.7T since 2019. Blunt cuts without restructuring invite chaos. Instead of slashing care for rural hospitals, target the $100B+ in annual improper payments and bureaucratic bloat.

New Hampshire’s providers are stuck cleaning up D.C.’s mess. Real reform means auditing every dollar, crushing fraud, and ensuring funds flow to patients—not administrative waste.

When bureaucrats treat Medicaid like a slush fund, rural communities pay the price.

Alzheimer’s caregivers face brutal realities—11.5 million unpaid family members sacrificing 18.4 billion hours annually while D.C. burns $360B on a broken system. The GUIDE model claims to fix this, but let’s be real: another federal pilot program won’t solve the core issue. Bureaucrats love throwing taxpayer cash at “coordination” while caregivers drown in costs, red tape, and sleepless nights.

If Congress actually prioritized efficiency, they’d slash administrative bloat in agencies like CMS and redirect funds directly to research and respite care.

Until then, it’s just more empty promises.

The real issue isn’t funding cuts—it’s systemic waste. Medicaid hemorrhages $55B annually through improper payments, duplicate programs, and ER misuse by non-citizens. Rural clinics struggle because bureaucrats prioritize bloated administrative costs over frontline care.

Fixing healthcare starts with auditing every dollar, enforcing eligibility checks, and cutting the fraud that’s bankrupting the system.

Blaming budget reductions ignores the rot at the core.

Congresswoman Goodlander’s bill highlights a critical disparity—military families shouldn’t pay premiums civilian plans don’t charge. TRICARE’s current policy forces dependents into costly Young Adult programs while civilian insurers absorb costs under ACA rules. The Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act aligns with Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) fiscal discipline, redirecting $1.6T in cuts toward strategic priorities like troop welfare.

Fixing this inequity isn’t expansion—it’s correcting bureaucratic oversight. Military families sacrifice enough without subsidizing D.C.’s inefficiency.

Streamlining coverage for 26-and-under dependents saves thousands annually, proving targeted reforms work when paired with broader spending discipline. Let’s fund defense properly—no more nickel-and-diming those who serve.

The numbers and policy details behind this reform demand attention—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/ATNUXUMSF0

The Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act (H.R. 2048) exposes a critical flaw in bureaucratic healthcare systems: forcing terminally ill patients to wait months for benefits they’ll never live to receive. While eliminating these cruel delays is necessary, it’s a band-aid on a hemorrhaging system. Medicare and Social Security already hemorrhage $1.7 trillion annually through fraud, overpayments, and administrative bloat.

This bill fixes one injustice but ignores the metastasizing tumor of government inefficiency devouring healthcare dollars. Every dollar saved by cutting wait periods should be matched by audits clawing back pharma overcharges and hospital price-gouging.

Real reform requires both compassion for patients and merciless accountability for the grifters bankrupting our system.
